title: Aniimo Complete Beginner Guide | Everything To Know Before You Start | Aniimo Guide
description: A complete beginner guide to Aniimo: platforms, starters, Twining, catching, combat roles, eggs, Homeland, Egg Heist and the best early habits.

sections.heading: Welcome to Idyll
sections.script: Have you started Aniimo yet? Aniimo is a free to play, open world creature catching RPG from Pawprint Studio, and it is one of the most talked about new games of the season. You explore a huge continent called Idyll, catch and collect creatures called Aniimo, build a home base and even merge with your creatures to explore the world. But with so many systems, a new player can feel lost in the first hours. In this beginner guide we go through everything you should know before you start: the platforms, the starters, the Twining mechanic, catching, combat roles, eggs, your Homeland and the multiplayer modes. Let's get you ready for your first steps as a Pathfinder.

sections.heading: Release, platforms and price
sections.script: First, the basics. Aniimo launched on September sixteenth, twenty twenty six, on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. On PC you can find it on Steam and the Epic Games Store. The mobile versions for iOS and Android followed one week later, on September twenty third. The game is free to play, with optional purchases, so you can try it without paying anything. It also supports cross progression, which means you can continue your adventure across platforms on the same account. That is perfect if you want to play on a console at home and keep going on your phone while traveling. If you play with friends, make sure everyone starts in the same place so you can meet up easily.

sections.heading: Choose your starter
sections.script: Early in the game you choose your first partner, and the choice is between two Light type Aniimo, Helion and Lunara. Both are good, so do not panic. The best advice is to pick the one whose look and playstyle you enjoy most, because you will spend many hours with it. Remember that the early fights are easy, and you will quickly catch many more creatures to build a balanced team. The game also teaches you the first catching steps in a short tutorial, which unlocks your first Aniipod, the tool you use to capture wild Aniimo. Do not rush through it. Listen to the explanations, because the same ideas come back again and again throughout your journey in Idyll.

sections.heading: Twining: the signature mechanic
sections.script: The feature that makes Aniimo different is Twining. When you Twine with a captured Aniimo, your Pathfinder physically merges with it, and you take direct control of its body and abilities. Depending on the creature, you can glide through the air, dig underground or sprint across the land. This is not only for fun. Some areas and puzzles in Idyll can only be reached when you Twine with the right kind of Aniimo, so a high level alone is not always enough. Before you judge a new catch by its combat strength, open the Aniimo management menu and look at its Twining abilities in the exploration tab. A creature that looks weak in a fight may be the key to a hidden chest.

sections.heading: How to catch Aniimo
sections.script: Catching is the heart of the game, and a few habits will save you many Aniipods. Crouch in tall grass and sneak up on your target, because an Aniimo that has not noticed you is easier to catch. Attacking from behind gives you a bonus to the catch chance. In a fight, fill the Break meter first, since a staggered Aniimo is much easier to capture. Weather and time of day change which creatures appear, so if the Aniimo you want is missing, come back at another hour or in different weather. Use the weakest Aniipod that works and save the Aniipod Ultra, which guarantees a catch, for rare or powerful targets.

sections.heading: Roles and elements in combat
sections.script: Combat in Aniimo is action based, so you dodge and attack in real time, and your team has five roles. A DPS deals the main damage. A Breaker drains the enemy's Break meter to stun it and open a window for bonus damage. A Support adds buffs and debuffs. A Healer keeps the team alive, and a Regen unit restores energy for longer fights. A simple plan is to open with your Breaker, hit hard with your DPS, and keep a Healer ready behind them. Elements matter too, because hitting a weakness deals extra damage. Do not build a team of one type only. Carry a mix of elements so you can switch when the situation changes.

sections.heading: Eggs and the Hatchinator
sections.script: New Aniimo do not only come from the wild. Eggs are an important source, and you find them in nests scattered around Idyll, often on rock pillars, trees and other high places. Some nests need a special Twining ability to reach, so keep exploring and come back when you unlock more skills. You can also earn eggs from chests, daily activities and the Egg Heist mode. To hatch an egg, place it in a Hatchinator, for example the one at the Outpost. Hatching runs on a real world timer, so you can keep playing while the egg develops. A good habit is to fill your Hatchinator slots before you go exploring, so no time is wasted.

sections.heading: Your Homeland and your RV
sections.script: Every Pathfinder has a personal RV, and through it you reach your Homeland. This is your personal space where you can plant crops, build decorations and arrange your Aniimo. As your RV levels up, more plots unlock, so keep upgrading it to get better farming, storage and production. Aniimo that live at home also do tasks, so a base is not only decoration, it gives you a steady supply of materials. A simple routine works well. Plant your fields, collect what is ready, spend your resources on upgrades and then return to exploring. Over time the Homeland becomes a relaxing place to rest between your longer expeditions into the wild.

sections.heading: Branches, bosses and exploration
sections.script: Idyll is full of things to discover. Bloom Branches are special points in the world. Activating one reveals more of the map, and spending Lumin Amber on it can improve catch rates in the area and give other bonuses, so it is worth finding them early. Wandering Alpha bosses are tough, but defeating them rewards you with large amounts of experience and valuable resources, and an Alpha Aniimo must be defeated before you can capture it with a special Aniipod. Do not forget the menus either. The event and tutorial tabs offer free rewards. Check them regularly, because free resources make the early hours much smoother.

sections.heading: Multiplayer and Egg Heist
sections.script: Aniimo is a social game too. Co-op supports up to four players, so you can bring friends to explore or fight tough enemies. The most competitive mode is Operation Egg Heist, a three player team activity in the Lost Isles, where you search, fight and race against other teams in real time to gather resources and rare eggs. It mixes the usual fights against creatures with player versus player battles, and a harder Chaos Mode was added later for experienced players. If you prefer a calmer pace, you can ignore it for now and focus on exploring and building. It is a great mode once your team is ready, and a good reason to log in with friends.

sections.heading: Ready to become a Pathfinder
sections.script: That is everything you need for a strong start in Aniimo. Pick a starter you like, learn Twining early, catch many different creatures, sneak up from behind, break your enemies, fill your Hatchinator and keep growing your Homeland. Most of all, enjoy exploring Idyll at your own pace. Now we want to hear from you. Which starter did you choose, Helion or Lunara, and which Aniimo is your favorite so far? Are you playing on PC, console or your phone? Tell us in the comments. If this guide helped you, like the video and subscribe for more Aniimo guides, and we will see you in the next one. Good luck, Pathfinder.
